messages:
incident-bot: INCIDENT: Elevated latency observed for /v1/generate across eu-west-1 and us-central-1 — p95 increased from ~220ms to 980ms at 14:03 UTC. Pagerduty triggered. @eng-oncall paging.

Alex K: I'm on pager — picking this up now. Noted multi-region, starts ~14:03. Any customer-facing alerts?

Marta C: Monitoring shows error rate stable, but request durations spike. Top affected path is /v1/generate (longer prompts). Linking dashboards: https://redwood.internal/dashboards/latency?range=30m

Priya S: Quick note: we shipped kernel 5.15.0-52 to a subset of infra earlier today for driver fixes. Rollout window 12:30-13:45 UTC. Could correlate.

Alex K: Good call — hypothesis 1: kernel rollout impacted scheduler/rt-preempt path for our inference nodes causing context-switch blowups. Hypothesis 2: tracing agent or new distro perf config causing overhead at tail latencies.

Jonathan R: Adding hypothesis 3: batcher/backpressure logic misfired and increased queueing leading to larger p95.

Alex K: Running quick perf + traces on a hot node (eu-west-1-gpu-34).

Alex K (code): ```sh
# top-level checks
ssh node@eu-west-1-gpu-34 'uname -a; cat /proc/cmdline; dpkg -l linux-image* | tail -n 3'
# perf sample
ssh node@eu-west-1-gpu-34 'perf stat -e context-switches,cpu-migrations -p $(pgrep -f redwood-runtime) sleep 10'
```

infra-bot: kernel.version: 5.15.0-52-custom; rollout_group: canary-2; drift_detected: false

Alex K: perf stat output: context-switches ~1.2M / 10s vs baseline ~120k, cpu-migrations ~140k vs baseline ~8k. That's a 10x increase in CS.

Sasha: That aligns with RT-preempt regression. Any dmesg logs?

Alex K (code): ```
# recent kernel logs
ssh node@eu-west-1-gpu-34 'dmesg | tail -n 80'
# sample lines
[14:02:58] warning: task redwood-runtime blocked for 300ms
[14:03:01] perf_event: interrupt took too long (2500 > 2000), lowering sample rate
```

Priya S: Also seeing elevated tracer spans on serve:trace where span.duration tail -> heavy serialization in epoll_wait? Trace snippet:
```
span: serve.handle_request  p50 18ms p95 910ms
child span: eventloop.poll p95 850ms
child span: inference.kv_cache_lookup p95 10ms
```
Looks like event loop stall, not model compute.

Jonathan R: Reproduced locally by toggling kernel preempt config on a dev node. When preempt disabled, eventloop.poll p95 drops back under 50ms.

Alex K: Immediate mitigation: rolling back kernel to 5.15.0-48 on one affected AZ to validate. Starting controlled rollback on eu-west-1-a (5 nodes) -> will observe p95.

Marta C: Noting customer impact: a handful of high-volume customers saw slower responses, but no timeouts. Support ticket counts +20% in last 30m. Escalating to CS for proactive messages.

infra-bot: rollback job queued: rollback/5.15.0-48 -> nodes [eu-west-1-a-1..5], job_id: rb-1923. Estimated 6m per node for reboot + health checks.

Alex K: Rolling...

(8m later)

Alex K: eu-west-1-a node-1 rolled back and rejoined. New traces show p95 ~210ms for that node's traffic.

Priya S: eu-west-1-a group p95 aggregated dropped from 920ms -> 230ms after 3 node rollbacks. This strongly implicates kernel change.

Sasha: Confirming perf counters also reduced: context-switches back to ~130k / 10s.

Jonathan R: Can we gather perf_events across a few pre/post nodes: perf top, schedstat, and ftrace of wakeups? I'll collect and paste snippets.

Jonathan R (code): ```sh
# schedstat baseline snapshot
ssh node 'cat /proc/sched_debug | sed -n "1,200p"'
# ftrace snippet
sudo bash -c 'echo function_graph > /sys/kernel/debug/tracing/current_tracer; echo 1 > /sys/kernel/debug/tracing/tracing_on; sleep 5; cat /sys/kernel/debug/tracing/trace | head -n 200'
```

Jonathan R: ftrace shows excessive wakeups in ksoftirqd and frequent task migration churn around redwood-runtime threads. Kernel commit linked to 5.15.0-52 introduced a scheduler tweak: https://kernel.internal/commits/abc123 (diff shows heuristics for idle balancing).

Alex K: Hypothesis status update inline:
- H1 (kernel rollout impact) — confirmed (evidence: perf counters, rollback -> latency drop) — owner: Alex K — status: confirmed
- H2 (tracing agent overhead) — unlikely (trace shows eventloop waiting on kernel paths, tracer overhead minimal) — owner: Priya S — status: ruled out
- H3 (batcher/backpressure) — no change in batch sizes observed; remains possible for unrelated regressions — owner: Jonathan R — status: low priority

Marta C: Customer impact list: cust-789 (high volume), cust-214 (medium) — CS notified for both; supportive mitigations applied (rate-limiting at edge for cust-789).

Alex K: Can we stop kernel rollout? infra team?

Priya S: Rolling halt issued across rollout pipeline. abort_pipeline id: kr-rollback-2026-03-15. Staging pause for further kernel deploys.

infra-bot: pipeline "kernel-canary" halted by Priya S (id kr-rollback-2026-03-15).

Sasha: Next steps for RCA: collect full per-node perf logs (perf stat, schedstat, ftrace samples), diff kernel config between versions (CONFIG_PREEMPT, CONFIG_NO_HZ_FULL), and reproduce in staging with same driver stack.

Jonathan R: I'm taking ownership of full trace collection + PR for kernel mitigation notes. Timeline to complete: 48h.

Alex K: Handing off oncall to Sasha for the night. Sasha — brief: rollback confirmed mitigated, kernel rollout halted, perf logs in /var/log/incident/1923456789/, CS notified, need to monitor for residual anomalies.

Sasha: Got it. I'll monitor dashboards until 04:00 UTC, will page if p95 > 400ms for more than 5min.

Pagerduty: On-call handoff completed: from Alex K -> Sasha at 15:12 UTC.

Marta C: Filing incident ticket INT-1923456789 with timeline and evidence. I'll attach perf artifacts and trace links.

Alex K: Thanks team. Final notes: do not re-enable kernel canary until kernel team confirms fix; consider pinning host kernel image for inference fleet until validated.

Sasha: Acknowledged. Will keep thread updated with any new spikes or rollback progress.

infra-bot: Incident state: mitigated (partial rollback) — monitoring.

(End of thread)
